proposed_comments.title: Preserve and revalidate the package's captured trust state
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve and revalidate the package's captured trust state

**Severity:** `critical`

The final check only compares package identity and verified-package metadata. For a target whose original package result was not verified, the code does not retain the full deployment and integrity state and can accept the same package identity after it becomes tampered, modified, stubbed, unavailable, external, mutable, or changes integrity state.

Capture the deployment and integrity fields in `PackageIdentity` after the initial package evaluation. During `IsCurrent`, repeat integrity verification whenever it was performed initially, compare the full captured state, and reject any state transition before activation.

**Verification:** Add focused tests showing that an unchanged approved-unverified package remains eligible while modified, stubbed, unavailable, external, mutable, or changed-integrity registrations fail revalidation.

confidence.rationale: The correction candidate captures and rechecks package state and rejects changed integrity and deployment transitions.

proposed_comments.title: Fail closed when the approved filesystem target is not namespace-protected
proposed_comments.body:
### Fail closed when the approved filesystem target is not namespace-protected

**Severity:** `critical`

For non-package targets, `IsCurrent` delegates to package revalidation, which treats an absent package identity as current. Absolute non-`.exe` paths, relative paths, and drive-relative paths such as `C:app.exe` can pass after approval without a retained file handle, and an executable handle alone does not protect writable ancestor directories that can be renamed before `ShellExecuteEx` resolves the path.

Distinguish URI targets from filesystem targets, reject every filesystem target without a retained file handle, and retain non-delete-sharing handles for each parent directory through the elevation request. Fail verification if any required directory cannot be protected.

**Verification:** Add regressions for absolute `.exe`, `.lnk` or script, relative and drive-relative paths, plus a URI case confirming legitimate protocol targets remain supported.

confidence.rationale: Absent package identity is currently accepted; the exact fail-closed correction and filesystem/URI regressions pass.

proposed_comments.title: Reject partially protected filesystem targets
proposed_comments.body:
### Reject partially protected filesystem targets

**Severity:** `critical`

When opening a parent directory fails, `Verify` returns an unverified target while retaining the executable handle. The current `IsCurrent` check only requires that file handle, so a user-approved warning can proceed without pinning the directory namespace that `ShellExecuteEx` later resolves.

Require the retained parent-directory handle set during filesystem revalidation, or clear the executable handle before returning from any directory-protection failure. Add a regression where a target has a retained executable handle but no protected directories and must be rejected.

confidence.rationale: The fresh Copilot loop confirmed the partial-protection path; the correction candidate requires directory handles and passes a focused regression.

proposed_comments.title: Avoid copying the launching-state map on each update
proposed_comments.body:
### Avoid copying the launching-state map on each update

**Severity:** `low`

`UpdateLaunchStatus` only reads the launching-state map before serializing it, but the new signature takes the map by value. Each update copies the full status map unnecessarily even though the call site already owns a stable snapshot.

Take `const WorkspacesData::LaunchingAppStateMap&` in the declaration and implementation so the UI helper does not create another full-map copy on every launch-status update.

confidence.rationale: The method only serializes the map and the const-reference correction compiles in the launcher project.

proposed_comments.title: Keep a termination fallback for the arranger process
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep a termination fallback for the arranger process

**Severity:** `medium`

The destructor now relies on the stored process handle for termination. If that handle lacks `PROCESS_TERMINATE` access, `TerminateProcess` fails and can leave the arranger process running even though the previous implementation reopened the process before terminating it.

When termination through the stored handle fails, reopen `m_processId` with `PROCESS_TERMINATE | SYNCHRONIZE` and retry before logging failure. This preserves the prior cleanup robustness while keeping the stored handle as the fast path.

confidence.rationale: The exact candidate restores a narrower termination fallback and compiles in WorkspacesLauncher.

proposed_comments.title: Format the UI termination Win32 error consistently
proposed_comments.body:
### Format the UI termination Win32 error consistently

**Severity:** `low`

The shutdown path logs raw `GetLastError()` when terminating the Workspaces UI process fails. That is harder to diagnose than the formatted Win32 error helper already used in nearby launcher code.

Include `common/utils/winapi_error.h` and log `get_last_error_or_default(GetLastError())` so the failure carries the same stable formatted diagnostics as the rest of the component.

confidence.rationale: Nearby code uses the same Win32 diagnostic helper and the exact candidate compiles in the launcher project.
